parsed.notes: No B-lens refutation found. Several records contain proposed negative progeny edges, but their disclosed treatment fields and scope notes do not downgrade the propositions reviewed here.

reasons: Lake treatment marks Illinois v. Caballes good_law as of 2026-06-30.
Scope note treats Rodriguez as a no-prolongation application and Jardines as a context boundary, not an overruling.
Lake identifies the input case as Navarette v. California and marks the anonymous-tip reliability point good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No point override supersedes the traffic-stop tip point.
Lake treatment marks Michigan v. Long good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No point overrides indicate the protective vehicle frisk rule has been overruled or superseded.
Lake treatment marks Delaware v. Prouse good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No point override limits the no-random-license-stop proposition.
Lake treatment marks Maryland v. Wilson good_law as of 2026-06-30.

Lake treatment marks United States v. Hensley good_law as of 2026-06-30.

Lake treatment marks Whren v. United States good_law as of 2026-06-30.
Scope note says the pretext-irrelevance rule has been reaffirmed throughout.
Lake treatment marks Kansas v. Glover good_law as of 2026-06-30.
Scope note confirms the narrow registered-owner inference and the negating-information limit.
Lake treatment marks United States v. Vinton good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No disclosed point override abrogates the D.C. Circuit protective-search treatment.
Lake treatment marks Heien v. North Carolina good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No point override supersedes the reasonable-mistake-of-law proposition.
residual_risks: Lake status is under_review and the scope note says S2 may re-derive/downgrade, but the disclosed treatment judgment remains good_law.

reasons: Lake treatment marks Devenpeck v. Alford good_law as of 2026-06-30.

Lake treatment marks Knowles v. Iowa good_law as of 2026-06-30.

Lake treatment marks United States v. Sharpe good_law as of 2026-06-30.

Lake treatment marks Florida v. Harris good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No point override supersedes the dog-alert probable-cause treatment.
Lake treatment marks Arkansas v. Sullivan good_law as of 2026-06-30.

Lake treatment marks Barnes v. Felix good_law as of 2026-06-30.
Scope note confirms the totality-of-the-circumstances rule and rejection of the moment-of-threat limit.
residual_risks: Lake notes the slip opinion is subject to formal revision, but not a treatment limitation.

Lake treatment marks Utah v. Strieff good_law as of 2026-06-30.

Lake treatment marks Maryland v. Pringle good_law as of 2026-06-30.

Lake treatment marks Terry v. Ohio good_law as of 2026-06-30.

reasons: Lake treatment marks Riley v. California good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No point override supersedes the digital-contents warrant rule.
residual_risks: Lake status is under_review and progeny enumeration is empty in the disclosed record, but the disclosed treatment judgment remains good_law.

reasons: Lake treatment for New York v. Belton is caution, not overruled wholesale.
Point override says the automatic vehicle-search rule is superseded/limited by Arizona v. Gant, and the page expressly says Belton is limited by Gant.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Frame Belton as surviving only within Gant's narrowed vehicle-SITA framework.

reasons: B-lens currency check: Delaware v. Prouse, Whren v. United States, and Rodriguez v. United States are each marked good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No disclosed treatment override contradicts the black-letter rule's live-law framing.
